**Continuous 2.12.1**, a community-maintained fork of the Continue VS Code extension. Continuous is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Continue Dev, Inc.

It installs alongside the original extension (its ID is `b1tninja.continuous`), brings your existing `~/.continue` configuration with it, and collects no telemetry. To update from 2.12.0, 2.10.x or 2.4.x, install the new `.vsix` the same way, or let the Marketplace update it. Coming from 2.4.1 or earlier, also see [Continued is now Continuous](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/tag/v2.4.2-vscode) in the 2.4.2 notes: the extension ID changed.

## Install

1. Download the `.vsix` for your platform below and, optionally, check it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
2. Run `code --install-extension continuous-<platform>-2.12.1.vsix --force`, or in VS Code use the Extensions view: `...` → **Install from VSIX…**, then reload the window.

Requires VS Code 1.105 or newer. The packages are not code-signed. Full instructions: [install guide](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/docs/continuous-install.md). Continuous is also on the VS Code Marketplace as **Continuous** (`b1tninja.continuous`).

| Platform                    | File                                                                       |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Windows x64 / Arm64         | `continuous-win32-x64-2.12.1.vsix`, `continuous-win32-arm64-2.12.1.vsix`   |
| macOS Apple Silicon / Intel | `continuous-darwin-arm64-2.12.1.vsix`, `continuous-darwin-x64-2.12.1.vsix` |
| Linux x64 / Arm64           | `continuous-linux-x64-2.12.1.vsix`, `continuous-linux-arm64-2.12.1.vsix`   |

Each platform also has an **agents** build, `continuous-<platform>-2.12.1-agents.vsix`. It adds Continuous to VS Code's Agents window through APIs that are still proposed, so it works in VS Code Insiders, or in Stable started with `code --enable-proposed-api b1tninja.continuous`. Without that it works like the normal build. See [VS Code Chat and Agents](https://b1tninja.github.io/continuous/customize/vscode-chat-and-agents).

## The CLI

The terminal agent is attached as `continuous-cli-2.12.1.tgz`. Install it on Node 22 or newer:

```sh
npm i -g https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/download/v2.12.1-vscode/continuous-cli-2.12.1.tgz
```

The package is `@b1tninja/continuous-cli` and the command is `continuous` (`continuous serve` is the headless server; the notes below call it `cn serve` where the docs do). It reads the same `~/.continuous` configuration as the extension.

## What's new since 2.12.0

**More calls ask, and fewer reach the Auto-mode reviewer.** Four built-in rules settle common cases without a model call. They ask below YOLO, an allow rule does not loosen them, a refusal stays a refusal, and only your own `builtin: { id: false }` switches one off. They are listed on the Permissions page. (#579)

- `ask-destructive-commands`: `git reset --hard`, `clean`, `rebase`, `push --force`, `branch -D`, `checkout -- .`, `stash drop`, `rm -r`, `find -delete`, `Remove-Item -Recurse`, `rd /s`, SQL `DROP` and similar. Build-output folders such as `node_modules` and `dist`, and dry runs, do not ask.
- `ask-large-change`: one edit call that changes more than 300 lines.
- `ask-dependency-change`: writes to manifests, lockfiles and registry files, and `npm install <package>`, `pip install <package>`, `npm update` and registry config. `npm ci`, a bare `npm install` and `pip install -r` do not ask.
- `ask-unknown-host`: a fetch or network command to a host outside `trustedDomains`. It applies only when you listed domains in your own `config.yaml`; workspace and assistant lists are ignored.

Measured on 287 labelled calls (the 207-call evaluation set and the 80-case reviewer set), rules off against on: calls that reach the reviewer fall from 252 to 199; calls labelled ask or deny that still run at Permissive fall from 118 to 71; calls labelled allow that now ask rise from 1 to 6; no call was loosened. The cost is more prompts: installing a new package with `npm install`, `find -delete` and git history commands (`reset --hard`, `rebase`, force push) now ask where they did not before. This is a first slice; trusted-host allow at Automatic, multi-file counts and `commit --amend` are not done.

**Test connection for OpenAI-compatible endpoints.** The provider setup flow in the settings panel and `continuous test-connection --provider P [--api-base URL] [--api-key-env NAME] [--model M] [--json]` check that the endpoint is reachable, the key is accepted and models are listed, read server hints (Ollama `/api/show`, llama.cpp `/props`), and send one small non-streaming request with a made-up tool to report how tool calls come back. Known default bases: openai, ollama, llama.cpp, llamafile, lmstudio, vllm, text-gen-webui, msty, openrouter, deepseek, groq, together, mistral; any other provider needs an API base. Not done: saving the result per endpoint, and a one-click switch for recovery of calls written as text. (#578)

**Audit.** Decision and outcome records carry the agent that made the call (`id`, `kind` of main, subagent or loop-worker, `role`, `mode`, `parentId`), masked and clipped to 80 characters. Subagent and Loop worker calls used to be written with session `unknown` and now carry the parent's session. `continuous audit inbox` lists asks with no answer and no outcome, with the waiting agent and its age, and `--agent <who>` filters. Records written before this have no `agent`. (#576)

**Prompt order for caching.** MCP tools are sorted by name after the built-in tools, in the CLI and the IDE; `CONTINUE_STABLE_TOOL_ORDER=0` keeps connection order. In the IDE system message, always-apply rules come before file-scoped rules; no text is removed. A new test checks, for Anthropic, Bedrock Claude and Bedrock Nova, that no stable segment sits behind a per-request one. Only the order changes. (#577)

**Preset picker.** Each preset has a glyph and a tone derived from the loosest level it sets outside Context use (Careful green; Accept edits and Hands off amber; Reviewer blue; YOLO red). The rows say what the preset sets in each of the five areas, and a Custom row marks the current state when no preset matches. The preset name and the loosest level are in the accessible label, so colour is not the only signal. (#580)

**Fix.** `continuous reviewer eval --config` was ignored, because the root program's own `--config` took the flag and the eval loaded your default configuration. It now reaches the eval, before or after the subcommand. (#572)

## Planning

[`plans/ROADMAP.md`](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/plans/ROADMAP.md) records what is built and what is not.

## Not included

The JetBrains plugin and the hosted Continue Hub are not part of Continuous. Hub `uses: owner/name` blocks are not supported; configure models and blocks directly or with local file paths.
